s1.syndrome_frame: A middle-aged woman with a long-standing breast lump and axillary discomfort
salient_findings: Mobile lump in the right breast
Migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
Multiple hypoechoic masses on breast ultrasonography
key_facts: No family history of breast cancer
Mobile lump palpated in the right breast
Breast ultrasonography revealed multiple hypoechoic masses
No obvious blood-flow signals detected within the lesions on color Doppler flow imaging

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with patient's age and presentation

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: common benign breast tumor, could explain mobile lump and ultrasonography findings

shortlist.label: Phyllodes tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rare tumor that can present as a mobile lump, ultrasonography findings consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ductal carcinoma in situ
shortlist.why_kept: pre-invasive cancer that can present with similar ultrasonography findings

shortlist.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: second most common type of breast cancer, can present with similar symptoms and ultrasonography findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a mobile lump, multiple hypoechoic masses with well-delineated contours on ultrasonography, and the absence of obvious blood-flow signals within the lesions are more consistent with fibroadenoma, a common benign breast tumor, especially given the patient's age and the long history of the lump.

rejected.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a harder, less mobile mass and often has increased vascularity on Doppler imaging

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Usually presents as a rapidly growing mass, which is not indicated in this 3-year history

rejected.label: Ductal carcinoma in situ
rejected.why: Typically does not form a palpable lump and is often detected by mammography as microcalcifications

rejected.label: Invasive lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: Often presents with a harder, more irregular mass and may have a more subtle appearance on imaging
